transcript.text: I need to flag something critical before we proceed. While reviewing the vendor's legacy contract archive, I found an anti-assignment clause in the original license that requires the vendor's prior written consent to transfer the software rights — and critically, the consent must specifically name the buyer as the permitted successor. The contract abstract that was circulated omitted this clause entirely, so it hasn't been reflected in our approval materials or the assignment draft. This means the vendor's signature on the assignment document alone may not be sufficient; the consent must expressly name the buyer. We need to address this condition before closing or we risk an invalid transfer of software rights.

transcript.text: I need to flag an operational gap. Yesterday I confirmed with the division's operations lead that the buyer requires uninterrupted access to the third-party software platform for exactly 120 days after closing while its replacement system is configured. This 120-day continued-access requirement has not yet been added to the transition schedule, and it directly intersects with Marcus's point — any vendor consent or assignment arrangement needs to expressly preserve the buyer's right to uninterrupted platform access for that full 120-day post-closing period, or the buyer faces a operational disruption during transition.
